evidence: RequestParsing.ts defines asRecord, requireString, requireNumber, requireArray and requireQueryString. Both OrderController.ts (parsePlaceOrder, listByState, advance) and ProductController.ts (register) use them, and neither controller has its own type checks.

ErrorMiddleware.ts keeps the only error-to-status table (STATUS_BY_KIND) and delegates to classifyError; no controller sets an error status itself. It also catches malformed JSON directly (isMalformedJson). That is a parsing error specific to Express, not a duplicate of the classification rule.

Persistence.ts (createInMemoryPersistence) is the single source of the repositories. CatalogueModule.ts (createProductController) and OrderModule.ts (createOrderController) both take a Persistence instead of creating their own stores.
HttpApp.ts (createHttpApp) mounts each controller through its routes() method and adds notFoundMiddleware and errorMiddleware in one place.
server.ts is the only place that creates RandomIdGenerator, SystemClock and the shared persistence, so the composition root is in one file.

InMemoryOrderRepository.ts, InMemoryProductRepository.ts, SystemClock.ts and RandomIdGenerator.ts each implement one port (OrderRepository, ProductRepository, Clock, IdGenerator) without adding unrelated work.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The infrastructure module serves one concern: adapting the application layer to the outside world. It has three kinds of file: adapters (in-memory repositories, SystemClock, RandomIdGenerator, HTTP controllers), wiring (CatalogueModule, OrderModule, Persistence, HttpApp) and the composition root (server.ts). The module's own building blocks are used consistently. Both controllers parse request bodies only through RequestParsing. Both feature modules get their stores only from the shared Persistence object. Mapping errors to HTTP status codes happens only in ErrorMiddleware via classifyError. Neither the parsing checks nor the error-to-status mapping is duplicated anywhere else in the module, and no file goes around these shared pieces.
